summary: @onereach/si-select preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package advertises itself as a Vue select input component but ships a preinstall hook that runs setup.mjs, which downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases (v1.3.13) into a temp directory, extracts it, marks it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB obfuscated @bun-cjs bundle using a rotating string-array obfuscator (WV8StW shuffle routine, _0x-style identifiers) whose purpose is not documented in the README or package.json. setup.mjs itself is obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style _0x identifiers and per-function string-lookup objects hiding plain strings such as 'ldd', '--version', 'musl', '/etc/os-release', 'Alpine', 'bun', 'bun.exe', the GitHub URL construction, and the execFileSync call chain, with only the sibling filename E="math_init.js" left in plaintext. A Vue input component has no legitimate need for a second language runtime; the fetch-alternate-runtime + execute-obfuscated-sibling shape at preinstall time evades Node-focused scanners and runs attacker-authored code on any machine that runs npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
